name: Deep Swamp Encounter Table
region: Swamp southwest of Nebruz — lizard-man territory
frequency: Check every 4 hours of travel or when the party makes significant noise

encounters.name: Quicksand
encounters.description: One or more PCs stumble into a treacherous sucking bog. No warning — the surface looks like solid ground.

mechanics.trigger: Each PC makes a Luck check (d20, roll under Dexterity) or stumbles in
mechanics.rescue: Rope or handhold extended to victim; rescuer makes Strength check DC 12
mechanics.retry: Check may be attempted multiple times; three consecutive failures — victim slips under and drowns
mechanics.osric_note: Use standard OSRIC drowning rules once submerged

encounters.name: Giant Leeches
encounters.description: The party fords a fetid creek. Colossal leeches attach before the party realizes they are under attack.

special: Attaches on successful hit — thereafter drains 1d6 hp automatically each round
Salt or open flame causes immediate detachment
Forcing off by hand deals an additional 1d6 damage to the victim

encounters.name: Insect Swarm
encounters.description: A massive stinging swarm descends on the party, drawn by the scent of blood or an open wound. Fills a 3" × 3" area.

osric_stats.ac: immune to normal weapons and non-area attacks
osric_stats.damage: 2 hp/round to all creatures within swarm area
special: Immune to normal weapons, missiles, and single-target spells
Fire, smoke, or area-effect spells disperse
All attack rolls at -2 while inside the swarm
Swarm pursues for 1d4 rounds if party flees

encounters.name: Alligator Ambush
encounters.description: A group of giant alligators waits motionless below the surface of a stagnant pool. The party must pass the pool's edge.

special: Surprise on 1-4 on d6 when submerged — party must make active Intelligence check against stealth to detect
Natural attack roll of 18+ means victim is dragged underwater — OSRIC drowning rules apply
Withdraw from combat into water at will

encounters.name: Giant Boa Constrictor
encounters.description: A massive constrictor lies coiled in the canopy above a trail. It drops on or grabs a PC or mount as they pass beneath.

special: Once constriction hits, automatically deals 2d4 hp every round thereafter
Constricted victim cannot attack freely — -4 to all actions
Escape requires Strength check vs. snake's Strength (treat as 18) or snake must be killed
NOTE: This is the quest creature — Leeandra needs the brain fluid; killing it is the objective

encounters.name: Will-o-Wisps
encounters.description: Pale lights drift through the reed beds, dancing just ahead of the party — leading toward open water or quicksand if followed.

special: Invisible at will — can vanish and reappear anywhere within 18" in one round
Immune to all spells except magic missile and protection from evil
Struck only by +1 or better magical weapons
Primary tactic: lure party into hazardous terrain (quicksand, deep water, alligator pools) rather than direct combat

encounters.dm_notes: Will-o-wisps detected and avoided by the party in session 27 — they know this threat exists.

encounters.name: The Debate
encounters.description: Three lizard-men at rest — not hunting, not working. The party comes upon them mid-argument. These are not members of an organization; they simply hold different views.
encounters.without_comprehend_languages: The party sees three lizard-men having what might be a dispute, a ritual, or nothing at all. Posture is tense but not aggressive. Interrupting clumsily risks violence.
encounters.with_comprehend_languages: A Clean Death argues measured patience — Leeandra vouched for these humans, the constrictor hunt serves everyone, interference is foolish. The Restrained Hunger isn't really disagreeing on logic; it keeps circling back to the same point without quite saying it. The Long Work says almost nothing, watches the reeds. The debate is not about the party specifically — it is about what the party represents.
encounters.violence_trigger: Aggressive movement, weapons drawn, or interrupting before the argument reaches its natural pause
encounters.dm_notes: This encounter rewards the spell. Without it the party gets tension and uncertainty. With it they get their first real window into the ideological fault lines.

encounters.name: Restrained Hunger Patrol
encounters.description: Two or three lizard-men block the path. Not attacking — but the air is wrong. They are still.
encounters.without_comprehend_languages: Three lizard-men in the path. They do not move. Their intent is unreadable.
encounters.with_comprehend_languages: Active internal debate: one voice saying not here, not Leeandra's errand. Another quieter, hungrier. The party has a window — name-drop Leeandra, show force, or back away slowly. Standing still while doing nothing lets the debate resolve badly.
resolution_options: Name Leeandra — immediate tension drop, they step aside
Show force without aggression (weapons visible, no advance) — standoff, then they withdraw
Back away slowly — they let the party go, follow at distance for 1d4 turns
encounters.violence_trigger: Advancing without acknowledgment, any aggressive action, or waiting too long without a response
encounters.dm_notes: Morale 9 reflects the internal tension — they want to fight but the restraint is real. If Leeandra is named they will not attack; she carries authority across all factions.

encounters.name: Long Work Engineers
encounters.description: A work crew of four to six lizard-men doing something strange — redirecting a creek, tending an egg nursery the size of a barn, or maintaining fish weirs. They ignore the party entirely.
encounters.without_comprehend_languages: A crew of lizard-men working. The work is alien — channels too straight, berms too even, structures too deliberate. They do not acknowledge the party. Threatening them or interfering with the work will bring a response.
encounters.with_comprehend_languages: Calm technical discussion. Water flow, load-bearing estimates, timelines measured in generations. One mentions a place name that might be Caelrun. Another describes a channel that will take forty years to complete. The work is entirely real and entirely unhurried.
encounters.violence_trigger: Interfering with the work, threatening the crew, or sustained presence without moving on
encounters.dm_notes: Morale 6 — they are not fighters by inclination and will withdraw if pressed, but interference with Long Work infrastructure will bring a larger response next encounter. The Caelrun reference is a slow-burn revelation the party may or may not register.

encounters.name: No Encounter — Landscape Beat
encounters.description: Roll d6 for which feature the party observes.

landscape_beats.description: A section of creek that bends at an angle no natural watercourse would take. The bank is shored up with packed clay and driven stakes. Old work. Settled.
A stand of dead trees hung with thousands of mud tubes — insect colonies the size of haystacks. A faint heat coming off them. Nothing moves, but something is alive inside.
Shallow pools separated by low berms, each thick with fish. The berms are too even. Someone built this and maintains it.
A clearing of churned mud, dimpled at regular intervals. Warm underfoot. Something is incubating below the surface. The party may not recognize it as a nursery.
A narrow channel running arrow-straight through the reed beds, disappearing into the mist in both directions. No obvious origin or end. Decades of work at minimum.
The remains of something very large, recently killed and mostly eaten. Clean work — little wasted. Something capable of taking down a creature this size lives nearby.
